main_body: A saddle drawn in side profile (pommel and cantle peaks with a dipped seat) on a two-legged stand
top_band: none. Down the middle column there is a thin dark brown seat-dip edge at about rows 12-13, then pale tan at rows 14-16. The tan is the saddle's side flap, a vertical face, not a horizontal surface.
evidence: The saddle is a side-view silhouette: raised pommel and cantle with a concave dip between them, and a flat tan flap with stud dots below. The seat is only a thin edge, so no horizontal surface is visible from above. The stand is two thin legs with no visible top face on any beam or base. This matches the 'side elevation chair' failure in the guide. There is no distinct front-edge line, eave shadow or recessed front.

style.evidence: The saddle has about 4 lightness steps (tan, light tan, mid brown, dark brown) plus two yellow stud dots and small studs. The outline is dark brown and tinted, which is fine. The tan flap is a large flat fill with no grain. The legs are flat 2-3 tone columns with no wood grain. The stall and well references carry far more tile detail and shading, so the candidate is clearly thinner and flatter.
